name: bunny — mesh stress + pen reference
comment: The Stanford bunny at full resolution (35,947 v / 69,451 tri) next to colors_widths, so a stress mesh and a known pen sit in one frame and the line lanes can be judged against each other. Measured release-native: 17.2 MB .pb -> 7.7 MB of GPU tables (1.4 verts + 0.8 indices + 4.0 edges + 1.6 markers) and ~122 MB resident above an empty scene, about 3.4 KB per vertex - the halfedge, not the render data. Under MESH_RAW_MIN (200k verts) so it keeps its wireframe and its vertex markers; armadillo and dragon in meshes.json are above it and draw faces only. The bunny is 0.156 units across natively, so the xform scales it to ~2 m; translation lives in slots 12-14, column-major. The Stanford models are authored Y-UP and this viewer is Z-up, so the scale carries a +90 deg rotation about X (column 1 becomes +Z, column 2 becomes -Y) - without it the bunny lies on its side.
